title: The partition of unity finite element method: Basic theory and applications
takeaway: Founding PoU-FEM paper: a PoU is used to glue LOCAL APPROXIMATION SPACES into a conforming global space; convergence inherits local accuracy. Key frame: PoU is an approximation/ansatz device — gluing solution spaces, not gluing different PDEs. Blending different physics is outside its guarantees.

title: The partition of unity method
takeaway: Companion theory paper. Error bounds require the PoU weights' gradients to be bounded by 1/diam(patch): wide overlaps = small weight gradients = small blending error. Direct analogue: seam width controls the extra terms PoU injects.

title: On the construction of blending elements for local partition of unity enriched finite elements
takeaway: The classic 'blending element problem': in the transition ring where enrichment is only partial, the PoU property is lost and PARASITIC (unwanted, non-representable) terms appear in the approximation, degrading convergence of the whole scheme. Fix = modified/enhanced blend elements. Lesson: the pathology of PoU coupling lives IN the blend ring, where neither description is complete.

title: A corrected XFEM approximation without problems in blending elements
takeaway: Standard fix: multiply the enrichment by a smooth ramp so it vanishes at the blend-ring edge — i.e., modify WHAT is blended (localize the special term) rather than sharpen the interface. 453+ cites. Supports 'modified PoU' over interface matching.

title: The Arlequin method as a flexible engineering design tool (orig. 1998 CRAS)
takeaway: Arlequin: two mechanical models coexist on an overlap; ENERGIES are blended by a PoU and the states are tied by Lagrange multipliers on the overlap. Rigorous way to superpose heterogeneous models — but needs an explicit coupling operator (weak matching), not just parameter mixing. The 'heavyweight' alternative if naive PoU seams misbehave.

title: On atomistic-to-continuum coupling by blending
takeaway: KEY NEGATIVE RESULT: PoU-blending two models' ENERGIES creates 'ghost forces' — spurious residual forces in the blend zone even when both models share the same homogeneous equilibrium neighbourhood; blending FORCES (the RHS) avoids ghost forces at the cost of variational structure. RD translation: blend the reaction RHS/wiring (vacuum-safe), and require the equilibria (vacua) to match — our iso-vacuum condition is exactly ghost-force removal.

title: Atomistic-to-continuum coupling
takeaway: Review of 20 yrs of blended a/c coupling: quantifies ghost-force error ~ |∇rho| of the blend function; smooth wide blends beat sharp interfaces; blended-ghost-force-corrected methods achieve optimal accuracy. Confirms: seam error scales with weight gradient — width is the control knob.

title: Composite overlapping meshes for the solution of partial differential equations
takeaway: Chimera/overset grids: subdomains solved on their own grids, coupled by interpolation in overlap zones. Works for smooth solutions; interpolation is NOT conservative.

title: A scheme for conservative interpolation on overlapping grids
takeaway: When conservation matters (shocks/steep fronts crossing the overlap), plain interpolation fails and special conservative interpolation is needed. Our one-grid PoU avoids this entire failure class: a single flux-form operator on one grid is conservative by construction.

title: On Schwarz alternating methods for nonlinear elliptic PDEs
takeaway: Schwarz overlapping iteration converges for classes of semilinear elliptic problems (incl. RD steady states). Nonlinear reaction terms are NOT an obstruction to overlapping decomposition per se — the theory just requires enough overlap.

title: Schwarz waveform relaxation algorithms with nonlinear transmission conditions for reaction-diffusion equations
takeaway: For semilinear RD, transmission conditions can (and profitably do) involve the NONLINEARITY itself; best interface operators are problem-adapted. Interface matching for nonlinear RD is a whole craft — a reason to prefer one-grid blending where no transmission condition is needed.

title: Optimized Schwarz waveform relaxation for advection-reaction-diffusion equations in two dimensions
takeaway: OSWR explicitly advertises coupling 'a different model in different subdomains' with adapted numerics per domain — the mature machinery IF we ever need different integrators per world. Overkill for same-integrator patchworlds.

title: A lateral boundary formulation for multi-level prediction models
takeaway: Davies relaxation: 50 years of production practice in weather models — a buffer zone of ~5-10 cells where the interior solution is NUDGED toward the exterior driving solution with a smooth ramp. Known artifacts: partial wave reflection at the buffer edges, over-specification noise; ramp shape/width tuning is empirical.

title: A tutorial on lateral boundary conditions as a basic and potentially serious limitation to regional numerical weather prediction
takeaway: Catalogue of buffer-zone pathologies: boundary-generated noise, sweeping-in of errors, dependence on ramp width vs dominant wavelengths. Empirical rule: the relaxation zone must be wide compared to the features crossing it — same rule we derived for blob tails vs seam width.

title: Bifurcations of front dynamics in a reaction-diffusion system with spatial inhomogeneities
takeaway: OUR OWN MODEL CLASS (Purwins school): spatial parameter inhomogeneities act on fronts as an effective potential; fronts pin to, oscillate around, or are transmitted past inhomogeneities depending on drive. The seam phenomenology we predicted (pin/drift/pass) is literally the 1995 result for this system family.

title: On the influence of inhomogeneities in a reaction-diffusion system
takeaway: Companion: localized parameter bumps act as attractive/repulsive centers for dissipative solitons — inhomogeneity = trap or scatterer. Predicts seams act on blobs as force fields (feature: fences/rails).

title: Front-bifurcations in reaction-diffusion systems with inhomogeneous parameter distributions
takeaway: Derives ODEs for front position in slowly varying parameter fields: front feels force ∝ local parameter gradient; drift-pitchfork unfolds. Gradient seams = smooth forcing ramps, no singular behavior for wide seams. Theoretical basis for 'seams are ramps, not walls'.

title: Heterogeneity-induced defect bifurcation and pulse dynamics for a three-component reaction-diffusion system
takeaway: THE three-component (our arch) heterogeneity paper: bump/jump heterogeneity in k1 creates defects that pulses hit -> penetration / rebound / pinning / oscillatory bound states, organized by saddle 'scattor' solutions; outcomes switch discontinuously with tiny parameter changes near criticality. Seams WILL have sharp regime boundaries — map them, don't average over them.

title: Dynamics of traveling pulses in heterogeneous media
takeaway: Review of the program: jump heterogeneities generate NEW stationary/oscillatory states localized AT the jump ('heterogeneity-induced ordered patterns', HIOPs); collisions of pulses with defects are mediated by hidden saddle solutions. Expect seam-localized blob states in patchworlds — a new object class, not a bug.

title: Heterogeneity-induced spot dynamics for a three-component reaction-diffusion system
takeaway: 2-D spots vs jump/bump/strip heterogeneities in the same 3-comp model: penetration, rebound, pinning, and traveling-along-the-jump ('sliding') — the seam-highway behavior we want is documented for spots in our architecture.

title: Pinned fronts in heterogeneous media of jump type
takeaway: Rigorous 3-comp FHN analysis: a parameter jump PINS fronts inside an explicit window of jump heights; existence+stability computable. Pinning threshold formalizes our |b_eff| level-limit intuition: small mismatch = transparent seam, large = fence.

title: Pinned solutions in a heterogeneous three-component FitzHugh-Nagumo model
takeaway: Extends to smooth (non-jump) heterogeneities: pinned solutions persist, positions selected by the heterogeneity profile. Smooth PoU ramps inherit jump-type phenomenology, just softened — width tunes force, does not remove it.

title: Wave-block in excitable media due to regions of depressed excitability
takeaway: Propagation failure ('wave-block') when a wave crosses into a region of reduced excitability: threshold behavior with explicit geometry dependence. Analogue: activity may simply refuse to cross a seam if the far side is sub-excitable — an intended fence use-case, but also a silent failure mode for 'transparent' seams.

title: Refraction and reflection of chemical waves
takeaway: Experiment: chemical waves crossing a boundary between media with different wave speeds REFRACT (Snell's law) and can totally internally reflect. Seams between RD worlds behave optically — expect refraction of blob trajectories and wave trains at seams.

title: Traveling periodic waves in heterogeneous environments
takeaway: Founding 'patchy habitat' RD theory: periodically alternating good/bad patches -> invasion speed set by patch statistics; propagation can FAIL if bad patches exceed a critical width. Patch-scale vs front-scale is the master parameter — same as our seam-width vs tail-length criterion.

title: Allee effects, invasion pinning, and species' borders
takeaway: Bistable invasion fronts PIN at habitat gradients: a species' range edge = front pinned by heterogeneity (364+ cites). Ecology's version of seam pinning; 'range boundaries' = stable pinned fronts at parameter ramps.

title: How individual movement response to habitat edges affects population persistence and spatial spread
takeaway: Habitat-edge RD theory: at an interface the correct matching can make the DENSITY DISCONTINUOUS (flux continuous, density jumps by a factor set by movement behavior/D ratio). Warns: continuity of u at a seam is a modeling CHOICE, not a law; different microscopic seam rules give different macroscopic seam states.

title: A role for ecotones in generating rainforest biodiversity
takeaway: Empirical ecology: ecotones (habitat transition zones) show divergent selection and elevated trait diversity — transition zones GENERATE novelty rather than just mixing neighbors. Biological precedent for 'ecotone evolution' as a productive operator, not merely an interpolation.

title: Pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems with piece-wise kinetic modulation
takeaway: Piecewise-constant kinetics: Turing stability is a LOCAL property per region; jump interfaces localize modes and select patterns; interface acts as effective boundary condition for each side. Supports treating each patch as its own world with local conditions + a seam layer.

title: Modern perspectives on near-equilibrium analysis of Turing systems (heterogeneity section)
takeaway: Review incl. heterogeneous Turing theory: for slowly varying parameters a WKB 'local dispersion relation' applies (space = frozen parameter); sharp gradients break it and can create instabilities with no homogeneous counterpart. Gives the quantitative regime split: seam width >> pattern wavelength => local-parameter picture valid (our PoU assumption); narrow seams => genuinely new modes.

title: From one pattern into another: analysis of Turing patterns in heterogeneous domains via WKBJ
takeaway: WKBJ machinery for RD with spatially varying params: modes localize where local Turing conditions hold; amplitude modulation + confinement predicted and verified numerically. The right analysis tool for predicting WHERE in a patchworld each species' texture lives.

title: Spatial heterogeneity localizes Turing patterns in reaction-cross-diffusion systems
takeaway: Extends WKB heterogeneity theory to cross-diffusion; heterogeneity gradients must be 'not too sharp' for the local theory — again the smoothness condition on seams.

title: Dissipative soliton excitability induced by spatial inhomogeneities and drift
takeaway: Dissipative solitons + inhomogeneity + drift => pinning/depinning saddle-loop bifurcations and EXCITABILITY of the soliton as a unit. A blob near a seam under a drift force is an excitable element — seams can turn passive blobs into spiking units (feature and hazard).

title: Diffusion in inhomogeneous media
takeaway: THE classic statement: for spatially varying D there is NO universal diffusion equation — dU/dt = div(D grad u) (Fick), = lap(D u) (Fokker-Planck), and D lap(u) are all legitimate limits of DIFFERENT microscopic dynamics. The PDE must be chosen from the physics, not from notation.

title: On the applicability of Fick's law to diffusion in inhomogeneous systems
takeaway: Pedagogical: Fick div(D grad u) preserves uniform states but implies zero flux at equilibrium even with D gradients; Fokker-Planck lap(Du) drives particles OUT of high-D regions producing nonuniform steady states from uniform ICs. Choice changes steady states qualitatively in ramp regions.

title: Fick and Fokker-Planck diffusion law in inhomogeneous media
takeaway: Microscopic derivation of when each law applies (position- vs bond-dependent jump rates). Confirms the trichotomy is physical, not numerical taste.

title: Homogenization of large-scale movement models in ecology
takeaway: 'Ecological diffusion' uses lap(D(x)u) deliberately: animals pile up where motility is low. Homogenization gives effective D = harmonic-type means. Ecology chose the NON-Fickian form on purpose — form encodes behavior at seams.

title: Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow (interface conductivity section)
takeaway: Standard practice for div(D grad u) with varying D: flux form with HARMONIC-MEAN interface conductivities preserves flux continuity across abrupt D changes; arithmetic-mean interface D overestimates flux at sharp contrasts. The correct discretization is the conservative flux form D_{i+1/2}(u_{i+1}-u_i) summed over faces.

title: Physics-dynamics coupling in weather, climate, and Earth system models: challenges and recent progress
takeaway: Multiphysics coupling review: ad-hoc blending/splitting between schemes creates spurious sources; conservation must be enforced by construction (flux coupling), not hoped for. Community consensus: blend STATES for smoothness, match FLUXES for conservation.

title: Analysis of ocean-atmosphere coupling algorithms: consistency and stability
takeaway: Air-sea coupling: commonly used lagged flux exchanges are INCONSISTENT with the true coupled problem (O(1) interface error unless iterated/Schwarz); stability and consistency at model-model interfaces is subtle even for linear diffusion. Warning for any future two-integrator patch scheme; irrelevant if we stay on one grid.

title: The two-regime method for optimizing stochastic reaction-diffusion simulations
takeaway: Coupling two DESCRIPTIONS of the same chemistry (Brownian/compartment) across an interface requires carefully derived exchange rules to avoid density artifacts at the interface; naive coupling leaves dips/spikes localized at the seam. Canonical demonstration that seam rules, not bulk physics, set seam artifacts.

title: Detached-eddy simulation (grey-area problem)
takeaway: Hybrid RANS/LES: the blend region ('grey area') between the two turbulence descriptions produces well-known artifacts (delayed instability, wrong stresses) because NEITHER model is valid in the blend. Generic lesson: in the blend zone you are simulating a third, unintended model — characterize it.

title: Analysis of gain scheduled control for nonlinear plants
takeaway: Gain scheduling = PoU over controllers/models. Guarantees hold only when scheduling variables vary SLOWLY relative to system dynamics; fast transitions void all guarantees. The temporal twin of 'seam width >> intrinsic lengths'.

title: Stability analysis and design of fuzzy control systems
takeaway: Takagi-Sugeno: blending N individually stable linear models with PoU weights does NOT imply the blend is stable; stability needs a COMMON Lyapunov certificate across the blend. Deep warning for patchworlds: two 'certified' worlds can have an uncertified (even unstable/cancerous) convex combination at the seam.

title: Finite basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs): a scalable domain decomposition approach
takeaway: PoU used constructively for PDE solving: solution = sum_i rho_i(x) NN_i(x) with smooth compact PoU windows; works because the PoU sum is the ANSATZ and one global PDE residual disciplines the seams. Generative PoU needs a global consistency signal (for us: the actual PDE integration provides it for free).

title: Finite basis physics-informed neural networks as a Schwarz domain decomposition method
takeaway: Makes FBPINN<->Schwarz correspondence exact; overlapping PoU windows = additive Schwarz. Formal bridge between 'blending' and 'domain decomposition' views: PoU composition IS an overlapping DD method with the overlap as seam.

title: Partition of unity networks: deep hp-approximation
takeaway: Learnable PoU partitions as an architecture; partitions themselves are trained. Precedent for putting rho(x) in the genome and letting selection move the seams.

title: Parameter-varying neural ordinary differential equations with partition-of-unity networks
takeaway: Closest generative precedent: dynamical-system PARAMETERS represented as PoU mixtures theta(x)=sum rho_i theta_i, learned from data, for hybrid/switching systems. Exactly our theta(x) = rho_A theta_A + rho_B theta_B — validated as a modeling ansatz in the ML literature.

title: Flow-Lenia: towards open-ended evolution in cellular automata through mass conservation and parameter localization
authors: Plantec, Hamon, Chan, Oudeyer, Moulin-Frier & Béna
takeaway: ALife's answer to patchworlds: make update-rule PARAMETERS a spatial field advected WITH the mass ('parameter localization'), so different rules coexist and MIX where creatures meet — multi-species worlds from rule mixing. Difference from us: their theta(x) moves with matter; our rho(x) is static geography. Both are PoU-in-space over rules.

title: Exploring Flow-Lenia universes with a curiosity-driven AI scientist
takeaway: Follow-up: automated exploration of Flow-Lenia's mixed-rule ecosystems; rule-mixing zones generate the interesting ecosystem dynamics. Evidence that parameter-mixing seams are where ALife novelty concentrates — 'ecotone evolution' already has an existence proof in a sibling system.

title: Texture regenerating and grafting using genome-driven neural cellular automata
takeaway: NCA grafting: spatially composing two trained NCA genomes in one grid; seams heal because each NCA is homeostatic. Small but direct precedent for compositing trained dynamical systems spatially.
